svg.title: Know every screen by its layout: what a screen fingerprint is, how it is made, how Localize uses it, when it says not sure, and how it stays fresh, in one image
svg.text: Know every screen by its layout
A fingerprint is a short code of a screen.
No picture to take. Any screen named in 11 ms.
A picture signature of one screen, stored on its node
The screen is greyed, shrunk to 17 x 16, and each cell is brighter than its left cell or not.
Details melt away. The layout stays.
Made when the node is saved
From the node screenshot, nothing to type
a tie with a sibling is refused
It is kept in the node data, next to the screenshot.
Saving a node that Localize could not tell from another asks you first.
The live frame against every reachable node
All 27 screens of a real map are compared in under a tenth of a millisecond.
One screen left: that is its name, with a confidence.
When it is not sure, it says so
An empty list is an abstention, never a guess
Unknown is a good answer. A wrong name would be worse.
A stored fingerprint is one frame
go to the node, prove it, save
The script recaptures every fingerprint-verified node of a tree.
A node it cannot prove is reported, never forced.
One check per node, once it works
an image or text check per node
Text checks still read a value, like a version number.
The focused tab or tile keeps its own focus check.
